name: volume_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when price breaks above the 1-minute range high with concurrent volume spiking more than 2x the 5-minute baseline, it signals that directional institutional program order flow is actively driving the move rather than passive market-maker adjustment. NIFTY's deep, continuous order book means that random noise rarely produces both range expansion AND volume elevation simultaneously — the confluence indicates genuine buying programs (FIIs, algos executing TWAP/VWAP orders) have overwhelmed the resting sell side. This institutional order flow typically sustains directional pressure for 30-60 seconds as the program continues filling, creating a predictable continuation window for ATM call/put entries.

indicators.name: range_high_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute high (12 bars x 5s) used as breakout reference. Original used 5-bar 1-min = 5 minutes, compressed to 1 minute because we hold 30-90s, not 5-15 min. A 1-minute micro-range captures the most recent consolidation zone; breaking above it with volume is a meaningful short-horizon signal. A 5-minute range would be too wide — NIFTY would need a 25+ point move to break it, overshooting our target.

indicators.name: range_low_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute low as bearish breakout reference. Same rationale as range_high_12.

indicators.name: avgvol_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute volume baseline (60 bars x 5s). Original used 10-bar 1-min = 10 minutes. Compressed to 5 minutes because at 5-second resolution NIFTY volume is more volatile — a shorter window adapts faster to intraday regime changes (e.g., lunch hour compression vs morning surge). 5 minutes is long enough to smooth noise yet responsive enough to capture the current session's volume regime.

conditions: close > range_high_12 (rolling max of high over prior 12 bars)
buy_ce.confirmation: Single-bar confirmation — both conditions on the same 5-second bar

conditions: close < range_low_12 (rolling min of low over prior 12 bars)
buy_pe.confirmation: Single-bar confirmation — both conditions on the same 5-second bar

exit.stop_rationale: NIFTY breakouts that fail typically retrace 8-12 spot points within 30 seconds; at delta ~0.5 that is 4-6 option points. A 4-point stop captures the false-breakout exit before the full retrace completes — if the breakout is failing, option premium drops 4 pts before the full 12-spot retrace.
exit.target_rationale: Genuine 1-minute range breakouts on NIFTY with volume confirmation extend 15-25 spot points (7.5-12.5 option pts at delta 0.5). A 6-point target captures the lower end of this distribution, achieving 1:1.5 R:R while maintaining a >50% hit rate on successful breakouts.

filters.vix_filter: none — volume surge already self-filters high-panic regimes
filters.time_filter: skip first 10 minutes (09:15-09:25) to avoid pre-open auction noise; flatten by 15:20
filters.trend_filter: none — volume breakout is direction-agnostic; buys CE on upside break, PE on downside
filters.spread_filter: none (limit order execution at close price)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — high-frequency algos increasingly trade the same signal; edge may compress but volume-confirmed breakouts retain a structural basis in institutional order flow

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from original: (1) Universe collapsed from nifty200 stocks to NIFTY index — the mechanism is cleaner on the index because NIFTY volume is driven by institutional program orders rather than earnings/news events, making volume surges more homogeneous in meaning. (2) Range lookback compressed from 5 x 1-min = 5 minutes to 12 x 5s = 1 minute, matching our shorter hold time of 30-90s instead of 5-15 min. (3) Volume baseline compressed from 10-min SMA to 5-min SMA at 5s bars to adapt faster to intraday volume regimes. Stop/target converted from percent-of-price to option premium points: original 0.5%/1.0% on a ~22,000 NIFTY = 110/220 spot pts, far too wide for 30-90s holds. Recalibrated to 4/6 option pts based on typical NIFTY 30-90s range extensions.
weaknesses: NIFTY volume data at 5-second resolution can be sparse/zero between ticks — avgvol_60 may be noisy
High false-breakout rate on days with low realized volatility (volume threshold may not suffice)
Simultaneous breakout signals (both CE and PE in quick succession) on choppy trending days
Volume surge may reflect expiry-related hedging rather than directional flow on expiry days
